items.title: US region
items.finding: West had the highest observed regional return rate (11.7%, n=1,611) versus South (2.9%, n=822).
items.association_not_causation: This is a descriptive geographic association in this US Superstore table. It does not identify an operational cause (mix, policy, or reporting differences could all contribute).

items.title: Prior returns and later orders
items.finding: Orders placed after at least one previous return had an observed return rate of 6.3% (n=774), compared with 5.8% (n=4,235) for orders with no previous returns. Two-proportion z = 0.54, p = 0.5887, risk ratio 1.09.
items.association_not_causation: This is an observational association. Previous returns may mark product mix, customer context, or other factors — they are not shown to cause later returns.

items.title: Discount at order placement
items.finding: The highest observed return rate among discount bins was 0–20% (7.5%, n=1,963). The lowest was >40% (4.2%, n=528).
items.association_not_causation: Discount bins can overlap with different products and promotions. The model may use discount as a correlate, not a proven lever.

items.title: Order value
items.finding: Among value bins, >$400 had the highest observed return rate (7.8%) and ≤$50 the lowest (3.5%).
items.association_not_causation: Order value is known at checkout; this does not imply that changing price would change returns.

recommendation: The model can flag higher-risk orders at placement for targeted review or customer-experience follow-up. It should not be used to automatically block customers. Any operational intervention (holds, outreach, policy changes) would need a controlled experiment / A/B test to estimate causal impact on return rate or cost. This project does not claim a percentage reduction in returns.
